Sentence Embeddings of Text

Source: R/sentence_embeddings.R
step_sentence_embeddings.Rd

step_sentence_embeddings() creates a specification of a recipe step that will convert a character variable into dense embedding dimensions by running each string through an embedding model.

Usage

step_sentence_embeddings(
  recipe,
  ...,
  role = "predictor",
  trained = FALSE,
  columns = NULL,
  engine,
  prefix = "sentembed",
  keep_original_cols = FALSE,
  skip = FALSE,
  id = rand_id("sentence_embeddings")
)

Arguments

recipe

A recipes::recipe() object. The step will be added to the sequence of operations for this recipe.

...

One or more selector functions to choose which variables are affected by the step. See recipes::selections() for more details.

role

For model terms created by this step, what analysis role should they be assigned? By default, the new columns created by this step from the original variables will be used as predictors in a model.

trained

A logical to indicate if the quantities for preprocessing have been estimated.

columns

A character vector of the selected variable names. This is NULL until the step is trained by recipes::prep.recipe(), and should not be set by hand.

engine

An engine object created by one of the embedding engine functions, such as embedding_custom(). The engine defines how strings are turned into vectors and holds the settings needed to do so.

prefix

A single string used as the prefix of the new columns. See Details for how the column names are built. Defaults to "sentembed".

keep_original_cols

A logical to keep the original variables in the output. Defaults to FALSE.

skip

A logical. Should the step be skipped when the recipe is baked by recipes::bake()? While all operations are baked when recipes::prep() is run, some operations may not be able to be conducted on new data (e.g. processing the outcome variable(s)). Care should be taken when using skip = TRUE, as it may affect the computations for subsequent operations.

id

A character string that is unique to this step to identify it.

Value

An updated version of recipe with the new step added to the sequence of existing steps (if any).

Details

Unlike step_word_embeddings(), which looks up and aggregates the vectors of tokens, this step takes a character (or factor) column directly and returns one dense vector per row, as produced by the embedding model. It doesn't use step_tokenize().

The new columns have names that begin with prefix, then the name of the variable being embedded, then the position of the dimension. For example, using the default prefix and a variable named text, the new columns are sentembed_text_1, sentembed_text_2, etc.

What is stored in the recipe

Embedding models are large, so the step never stores the model. It stores the engine, which is a reference to the model, together with the number of dimensions seen when the recipe was prepped. This keeps prepped recipes small, but it also means a prepped recipe can only be baked where the engine can run. A recipe that is moved to another machine needs whatever the engine depends on to be available there.

If the engine returns a different number of dimensions when baking than it did when prepping, bake() errors instead of returning columns the downstream model wasn't trained on.

Missing values and caching

Missing values stay missing: a row with NA text gets NA in all of its embedding columns, and is never sent to the engine. Empty strings are sent to the engine as they are.

Embedding is usually the slowest part of a recipe, and bake() embeds new data every time it is called. Within an R session, embeddings are cached per engine and string, so repeated strings, and the training data that is embedded both by prep() and by bake(), are only embedded once. The cache lives outside the recipe and is cleared when the R session ends.

Tidying

When you tidy() this step, a tibble is returned with columns terms, engine, model, revision, dimension, and id:

terms

character, the selectors or variables selected

engine

character, the name of the engine

model

character, the name of the model, NA if the engine doesn't have one

revision

character, the version of the model the engine is pinned to, NA if the engine can't pin one

dimension

integer, the number of embedding dimensions, NA until the recipe is prepped

id

character, id of this step

Case weights

The underlying operation does not allow for case weights.

See also

embedding_custom() for the available engines, and step_word_embeddings() for embeddings that are aggregated from tokens.

Other Steps for Numeric Variables From Characters: step_dummy_hash(), step_sequence_onehot(), step_textfeature()

Examples

library(recipes)

# A toy embedder, replace it with a call to a real embedding model
toy_embedder <- function(x) {
  cbind(
    nchar = nchar(x),
    vowels = nchar(gsub("[^aeiou]", "", x))
  )
}

sample_data <- tibble(
  text = c("The cat.", "The cat ran.", "A longer sentence here."),
  text_label = c("short", "short", "long")
)

rec <- recipe(text_label ~ ., data = sample_data) |>
  step_sentence_embeddings(text, engine = embedding_custom(toy_embedder))

obj <- rec |>
  prep()

bake(obj, new_data = NULL)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 3
#>   text_label sentembed_text_1 sentembed_text_2
#>   <fct>                 <dbl>            <dbl>
#> 1 short                     8                2
#> 2 short                    12                3
#> 3 long                     23                7

tidy(rec, number = 1)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 6
#>   terms engine          model revision dimension id                    
#>   <chr> <chr>           <chr> <chr>        <int> <chr>                 
#> 1 text  custom function NA    NA              NA sentence_embeddings_j…
tidy(obj, number = 1)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 6
#>   terms engine          model revision dimension id                    
#>   <chr> <chr>           <chr> <chr>        <int> <chr>                 
#> 1 text  custom function NA    NA               2 sentence_embeddings_j…
